newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan urged to tighten economic policy on China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan urged to tighten economic policy on China.

text.p: The board of Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council has proposed the government tighten its controls on outflows of liquidity and high-technology investments to China, the United Daily News newspaper reported on Sunday.
Taiwan bans direct contact of any kind with China after a civil war separated the two in 1949. All investments must be routed through a third region on a case-by-case basis with government approval.

Chan Hung-chih, a director of the council which sets guidelines for the island's policy towards China, said board members also suggested that the government thoroughly review the growth in its economic relations with China in the past few years to ensure the island's economic independence, the newspaper reported.
Since a political thaw began in the late 1980s, some 25,000 Taiwanese businesses have poured over US$20 billion into China.

President Lee Teng-hui, worried that the island would become too dependent on China, said last August that the island needed to review its policy of targeting China as its main market and avoid over-dependence on the mainland for investments.
